briefs.headline: NBFCs overtake housing as biggest driver of bank credit
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Banks lent more to NBFCs than to home buyers in the first half of FY27, with advances to non-bank lenders rising by Rs 1.8 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.4 lakh crore for housing. Of the Rs 16.1 lakh crore incremental non-food credit added between March 31 and Sept 30, industry accounted for Rs 3.7 lakh crore, while trade absorbed Rs 1 lakh crore, reflecting strong demand across corporate and services segments.
Scheduled commercial banks' outstanding non-food credit rose 19.1% year on year to Rs 229 lakh crore at the end of Sept, with the six-month expansion marking a 7.5% increase over March. Services accounted for the largest share of incremental lending at Rs 4.9 lakh crore, followed by personal loans at Rs 4.5 lakh crore, industry at Rs 3.7 lakh crore and agriculture at Rs 1.8 lakh crore.
Gold loans continued to be a major contributor to retail credit growth. Outstanding advances against gold jewellery surged 82.6% year-on-year to Rs 5.8 lakh crore, rising 25.1% in the first half alone. Banks added Rs 1.2 lakh crore in gold loans between March and Sept.
Clooneys' foundation gives free legal aid to over 9,000 women and children
Within services, lending to NBFCs grew 41.8% year-on-year to Rs 22.5 lakh crore. Commercial real estate advances rose 23.3% to Rs 7.5 lakh crore, while trade credit grew 23.9%. Services credit as a whole expanded 28.3% to Rs 64.9 lakh crore, accounting for 30.6% of incremental non-food lending.
Industrial credit grew 19.5% to Rs 49.8 lakh crore. While advances to large industries rose 16% to Rs 33 lakh crore, lending to medium enterprises grew 33.2% and to micro and small enterprises 24.4%. Of the Rs 3.7 lakh crore incremental industrial credit, large companies accounted for Rs 2 lakh crore and MSMEs Rs 1.6 lakh crore.
Agriculture and allied activities credit rose 19.5% to Rs 28.2 lakh crore from Rs 23.6 lakh crore a year earlier. Personal loans grew 17.3% to Rs 74.27 lakh crore, although the composition of retail lending shifted towards secured advances.One of the fastest-growing segments was loans against fixed deposits, including FCNR(B) and NRNR deposits. Outstanding advances in this category rose 53.3% year-on-year to Rs 2.2 lakh crore, increasing 28.1% in the six months to Sept. Banks added Rs 47,471 crore in such loans during the period.
These advances accounted for 10.6% of the Rs 4.5 lakh crore incremental personal loans during the half-year and 3% of the banking system's incremental non-food credit.

briefs.headline: AU Bank probes potential data leak
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data leak involving a Salesforce-hosted software platform that holds limited information relating to its vehicle loan customers, after a cyber threat intelligence platform flagged claims by a hacking group that it had breached the lender's systems. The bank said the incident involved a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform managed and hosted by Salesforce.
"We reaffirm that the Bank's own systems remain unaffected and all banking services are operating normally," a bank spokesperson said. HackRisk.io, a threat intelligence and cyber-attack monitoring platform, flagged the alleged breach in a post on X on Oct 29. The ScarlettGroup hacking group claimed to have accessed sensitive customer and internal corporate data and threatened to release it. According to hackers' claims, the compromised information includes KYC records.

briefs.headline: Nasdaq bleeds: Faces $2 trillion wipeout in October
briefs.bodyText:
More than $2 trillion in market value is set to be wiped from the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 this month, as Big Tech earnings intensified investor scrutiny of whether the billions being poured into artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough.
The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX's entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8% so far in Oct as the AI trade ran into turbulence, with hyperscalers Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Amazon.com raising spending forecasts further as they race to expand AI infrastructure.
The prospect of ever-bigger AI outlays has unnerved investors, particularly as rising borrowing costs threaten to make debt-funded investment more expensive and harder to justify.
Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage drop on record on Thursday after disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn. Meta's plans for a record $97.5 billion fund raise heightened concerns about shareholder dilution and whether mounting AI spending could force other Big Tech companies to increasingly tap capital markets.
Nasdaq 100 set to lose over $2 trillion in October as rising AI spending fuels investor concerns
On Friday, Intel's stock led the way lower and was flirting with its worst day since 1974 after tumbling 30%.
Microsoft and SpaceX broke from the gloom, with results that showed AI spending starting to pay off.
"It may be that we've overestimated how strong the growth might be, but they're not going negative in aggregate," said John Bilton, global head of strategic research at Multi-Asset Solutions.
"We have an insatiable and growing demand for data." Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise about $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years. Among other hyperscalers, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in bond sales over the past four years, worrying investors about overreliance on the medium for raising capital. Morgan Stanley forecast capital spending on AI infrastructure overall will surpass a trillion dollars next year. AI companies' growing reliance on debt funding is emerging as a new risk for investors, challenging the view that the companies at the heart of the boom are insulated from macroeconomic pressures.
The concern is spreading beyond stocks to credit markets, where investors are starting to price in the possibility that rising financing costs, combined with slower returns on AI spending, could squeeze companies previously viewed as relatively insulated. Revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has remained strong since ChatGPT's launch in 2022, showcasing insatiable demand and perhaps why investors were initially willing to back the spending, even as the timeline of payoffs remains uncertain.
Amazon's cloud computing cash cow, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, while Meta offered better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook. Microsoft also forecast strong cloud growth in its latest earnings report.
Big Tech has historically spent heavily on infrastructure to build and expand businesses such as cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce, but the AI boom has pushed capital expenditure to dizzying levels. JP Morgan expects global AI capex to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, and sees $900 billion being spent in 2026 alone. Reuters

briefs.headline: Power, fertiliser fuel LNG import surge
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's LNG imports rose 17.4% to a record 2.7 million tonnes so far in Oct on the back of higher demand from the power, fertiliser and city gas distribution sectors. Besides, more cargo arrived from Qatar and the UAE, data from maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler showed.
Crude imports also reached a record 5.6 million barrels per day (mbd) during the month, 14% higher than a year ago, with Russia remaining the top supplier, while shipments from West Asia and the Atlantic Basin also rose.
LNG supplies increased as India's domestic production has declined, pushing up the import dependence from 50% to nearly 52%. In addition, companies are seen to be stocking up the gas for the power sector, as solar energy is set to decline in winters, and the fertiliser sector will need higher feedstock for production.
Crude imports also touch a record 5.6 million barrels per day in October, with Russia retaining its position as the top supplier despite declining shipments.
According to Kpler data, the record LNG imports in Oct can be attributed to a sharp rebound in supplies from Qatar, which had remained curtailed due to disruptions in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz during the West Asia conflict. Qatar has traditionally been the biggest supplier of LNG to India, accounting for 40-50% of total imported volumes. In Sept last year, India imported nearly 2.1 MT of LNG, of which 0.8 MT came from Qatar.
 India received more than 0.4 MT of LNG from Qatar this month, the highest volume since the war broke out. The supplies were 370% more than the 0.1 MT received from the West Asian nation in Sept, and only marginally lower than the cumulative imports between March and Sept.
Despite its production facilities being impacted, sources said Qatar was willing to increase LNG supplies and meet its long-term commitments to customers.
The US, however, continued to remain the biggest supplier of LNG, with 0.6 MT of supplies till Oct 29. The UAE, Oman, Angola, Nigeria and Australia were other major suppliers during the month. Though Russian crude flows have declined from a peak of 2.8 mbd in July to nearly 2 mbd in Oct, Moscow remained the largest supplier, accounting for nearly 36% of total imports.
Nikhil Dubey, Kpler's lead analyst - refining, however, said elevated freight costs of Russian barrels had eroded their delivered-price advantage, while improved supplies from West Asia offered competitive alternatives to refiners. He said supplies from Gulf countries stood at around 2.3 mbd in Oct, compared with 2.7 mbd in Sept, with Saudi Arabia leading the pack, followed by Iraq.

briefs.headline: Trai proposes draft framework for responsible use of AI in tele networks
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Trai on Friday proposed a comprehensive draft framework for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in telecom networks that would require service providers to adopt board-approved AI policies, establish dedicated governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents to the regulator.
The draft guidelines, released for stakeholder consultations, also seek to make entities accountable for the outcomes of AI systems deployed in their networks and services, "irrespective of whether AI systems are developed internally, procured/ outsourced from a third party or a combination thereof."
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
 (Trai), in a release, said it has floated the "draft 'Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services' for stakeholders' comments". Agencies

briefs.headline: Govt sets up committee to reform banking sector
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt Friday set up a high-level committee under former central vigilance commissioner Suresh N. Patel to undertake comprehensive banking reforms, delivering on an announcement made by finance minister 
Nirmala Sitharaman
 in Union budget 2026-27.
The five-member panel, which includes RBI deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, former RBI deputy governor N S Vishwanathan, former Indian Bank MD & CEO Padmaja Chunduru alongwith a finance ministry representative, has a tenure of six months to submit a roadmap aimed at reforms necessary to make Indian banking "globally competitive, financially inclusive, and resilient for Viksit Bharat, 2047," said govt.
The panel's mandate spans "structural, institutional, regulatory, and legislative" overhauls across commercial banks, regional rural banks (RRBs), cooperative institutions, and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Besides assessing long-term capital needs for banks and development financial institutions (DFIs) to spur private investment, the committee will evaluate priority sector lending norms, cybersecurity frameworks, AI adoption, and talent acquisition strategies.
This step marks the latest major structural review of the banking sector after Narasimham committee (1998) laid the foundation for tightening capital adequacy ratios and non-performing asset (NPA) norms, in the wake of 1991 liberalisation reforms.
Later, Raghuram Rajan committee (2008) advocated incremental structural shifts to expand credit access and financial markets, while Urjit Patel Committee (2014) advocated for inflation targeting by setting up the monetary policy committee.

briefs.headline: Reliance Industries Q2 net rises 34% to Rs 29,550 crore
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Reliance Industries, India's most valuable company by market capitalisation, reported a 34% rise in second-quarter profit for FY27 to Rs 29,550 crore on Friday, beating analysts' average estimate of Rs 21,419 crore. The increase was driven by strong performance at its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) and Jio digital services businesses. Revenue increased 29% to over Rs 3.3 lakh crore, while ebitda climbed 26% to Rs 61,224 crore. Expenses rose 28% to Rs 3 lakh crore.
RIL CMD 
Mukesh Ambani
 said the O2C business delivered a particularly strong performance in the quarter, led by tight fuel markets, improved petrochemical margins and firm domestic demand.
Ebitda at the O2C division, which accounted for 41% of total operating profit, jumped 68% year-on-year to Rs 25,203 crore. Stronger transportation fuel and downstream margins drove the gain.
Jio Platforms, which made a blockbuster stock market debut this week, posted an 18% rise in ebitda to Rs 22,223 crore on strong revenue growth, operating leverage and a 250-basis-point margin expansion. Average revenue per user rose nearly 4% to Rs 219, helped by a better subscriber mix and increased usage, partly offset by broadband promotions.
Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance posts 34% growth in Q2 profit, with revenue crossing Rs 3.3 lakh crore; board approves Rs 15,000 crore fundraising plan
Ebitda at the retail unit fell 10% to Rs 6,120 crore, even as revenue grew 6% to Rs 80,220 crore in the second quarter of FY27. RIL said performance was affected by the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.
Ebitda at the oil and gas division slipped 2% to Rs 4,901 crore due to lower revenue and higher govt levies. Ebitda from smaller businesses, including media and consumer products, was flat at Rs 2,777 crore.
RIL had a cash balance of over Rs 2.6 lakh crore, comfortably covering net debt of Rs 1.2 lakh crore. Capital expenditure totalled Rs 38,153 crore, largely driven by investments in O2C and new energy projects, and by the expansion of infrastructure and distribution networks of its consumer businesses.
The RIL board on Friday approved a plan to raise Rs 15,000 crore through listed, redeemable non-convertible debentures.
"This week marked a historic moment in Reliance's value creation journey with Jio's record-setting listing on Indian bourses. It demonstrates the depth of confidence investors place in Jio's solid foundation and strong growth visibility.
"I am proud to witness the rejuvenation of "the equity cult" originally pioneered by our founder-chairman during the 1977 Reliance IPO," said RIL chairman Mukesh Ambani.

briefs.headline: IOC profit surges 2.7x in Q2 on crude price decline
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: State-run 
Indian Oil Corporation
 (IOC) reported record profit of Rs 22,503 crore during the Sept quarter - a 2.7-fold jump over a year ago - driven largely by a decline in crude oil prices between July and mid-Aug and robust margins from the petrochemical and gas segments. In the June quarter, the company had reported a loss of Rs 1,241 crore due to elevated crude prices amid the West Asia war. IndianOil, however, warned that profitability in the upcoming quarters may again be impacted by inventory losses if crude oil prices fall with the normalisation of the situation in West Asia.
The company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 30% to Rs 2.7 lakh crore in Q2FY27, from Rs 2.1 lakh crore in Q2FY26. For the first half of FY27, IOC reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 21,361.5 crore, up 42% from Rs 14,999 crore in April-Sept FY26.

stories.headline: Rohit Sharma likely to lead Mumbai Indians again, Tilak Varma could be deputy
stories.deck: As the Mumbai Indians strategize for IPL 2027, they are contemplating bringing Rohit Sharma back as captain while also considering trading Hardik Pandya to another team. With Kieron Pollard leading a revamped coaching staff that includes Robin Uthappa and T Dilip, MI aims for a turnaround after finishing ninth in the previous season.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Will Rohit Sharma return as Mumbai Indians captain, with India’s rising T20 batting star Tilak Varma as his deputy, in IPL 2027? TOI has learnt that there is a strong possibility of the 39-year-old getting one final stint at the helm. Rohit led MI to all five of their IPL titles — in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020.
A return to the captaincy would mean Rohit cannot feature as an Impact Player, as he has done over the past two seasons. Meanwhile, Hardik Pandya, who replaced Rohit as captain in 2024, is set to be traded to another franchise.
MI are in talks with three teams, with an official announcement expected soon, TOI has learnt.
MI on Friday announced a major overhaul of their coaching staff under newly appointed head coach Kieron Pollard. Former India batter Robin Uthappa has been named batting coach, while former India fielding coach T Dilip will take charge of the fielding department.
Uthappa represented MI in the inaugural IPL season in 2008, while Dilip spent nearly five years with the Indian team and is believed to share a close rapport with Rohit.
MI have also brought back two former pacers — New Zealand’s Mitchell McClenaghan as bowling coach and Dhawal Kulkarni as development bowling coach. 
Kulkarni, a former India and Mumbai teammate of Rohit, will have a year-round role focused on player development and strengthening the franchise’s talent pool.
The appointments, with several members of the new support staff having close links with Rohit, have further fuelled speculation about his return to the captaincy as MI look to end their six-year title drought. The franchise last won the IPL in 2020 and finished ninth in 2026. The new coaching group’s immediate task will be to finalise retentions ahead of the mini-auction for IPL 2027, scheduled for Dec 16 in Goa. Pollard and his team will also have to formulate their auction strategy as MI seek to rebuild after a disappointing 2026 campaign.

stories.headline: Rickelton, Mulder tons help SA set 288-run target for Aus in series decider
stories.deck: South Africa's position in the third Test appears formidable, with centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder contributing to a second innings total of 387. Australia now faces a daunting chase of 288 runs to secure the series, level at 1-1. The final day is expected to present tricky batting conditions, and Simon Harmer's spin bowling could prove crucial in this intense encounter.
stories.bodyText:
Centuries from 
Ryan Rickelton
 and Wiaan Mulder put South Africa in a commanding position against Australia in the series-deciding third Test at Newlands on Friday, setting up an intriguing final day's play.
South Africa, who began the fourth day with a slender 40-run lead and six wickets in hand, finished their second innings on 387, stretching their advantage to 287 runs. Australia now need 288 on the final day to win the three-Test series, which is currently level at 1-1.
Rickelton (101 off 219 balls) and Mulder (115 off 221 balls) led South Africa's recovery with a crucial sixth-wicket partnership worth 154 runs. The pair spent nearly 54 overs together, frustrating the Australian bowlers and forcing the visitors to turn to as many as eight bowling options.
South Africa were 140/4 overnight and lost Matthew Breetzke in the morning session, caught at fine leg off Pat Cummins. The Australian captain's breakthrough ended a wicketless spell of more than 62 overs stretching back to the first Test in Durban.
Rickelton and Mulder then took charge, adding 92 runs during the second session without losing a wicket. Rickelton reached his half-century off 105 deliveries, while Mulder went into the tea break unbeaten on 46. 
Their partnership crossed the 100-run mark after 193 balls.
Australia managed to slow the scoring after tea, conceding just 13 runs in 10 overs, but the South African duo continued to build their lead. Rickelton eventually completed his third Test century off 219 balls, striking 12 boundaries. It was also the first century by a South African batter at No. 6 in the third or fourth innings of a Test since 2022.
The partnership ended in unfortunate fashion when Mulder ran out Rickelton after sending him back too late. South Africa then suffered a brief collapse, losing four wickets for just 16 runs, with Gerald Coetzee also falling to a run-out after a mix-up involving Mulder.
With the lower order exposed, Mulder took responsibility and shifted gears. Having taken 138 balls to reach his first 50, he needed only another 66 deliveries for his second half-century. He brought up his fourth Test hundred off 204 balls and finished with 10 fours and four sixes before falling to Cummins in the deep while attempting a pull shot.
Mitchell Starc was Australia's most successful bowler in the innings, claiming 3/65 to take his match tally to nine wickets.
Australia face a challenging chase on the final day, with Newlands having witnessed a successful fourth-innings target of 331 only once, when Australia achieved it in 2002. South Africa will also draw confidence from a pitch expected to offer increasing assistance to spinners and the presence of an in-form Simon Harmer, who was rested earlier in the match.
The visitors have the entire fifth day to chase 288 and clinch the series, while South Africa will look to defend their total.

stories.headline: Delhi HC asks WFI to decide in two weeks show-cause notices to Vinesh Phogat
stories.deck: Justice Amit Mahajan, in an order passed on October 29 on Phogat's petition, said that the decision on the notices issued on May 9 and June 17 would be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing on January 20
stories.bodyText:
The Delhi High Court has asked the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) to decide two show-cause notices issued to grappler Vinesh Phogat over allegations of violation of anti-doping rules and misconduct in two weeks.
The court, in an order passed on October 29 on Phogat’s petition, said a sportsperson has to be mentally relaxed to participate in any competitive event and clarified that the decision on the notices issued on May 9 and June 17 would be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing on January 20.
“A sportsperson has to be in a fit and relaxed state of mind to participate in any competitive event of such nature as indicated so that their performance is not compromised in any way,” the court said.
“In view of the same, the respondents are directed to take a decision on the impugned SCNs (show-cause notices), within a period of two weeks. If the decision is taken, after two weeks, the same shall be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing. List on January 20, 2027,” the court ordered.
The court was hearing Phogat’s petition seeking quashing of the two show-cause notices issued to her by the WFI over allegations of indiscipline and violation of anti-doping rules, and disciplinary proceedings initiated against her.
Her counsel said she wished to participate in a national tournament scheduled to be held sometime in the middle of December, and the show-cause notices were “kept as a hanging sword” over her.
In the plea, Phogat said that the two notices issued to her on May 9 and June 17 are part of a “continuing pattern of arbitrary and mala fide action” by the WFI, obstructing her return to competitive wrestling after maternity.
In the May 9 show-cause notice, the WFI declared Phogat ineligible to participate in all WFI competitions and events until June 26, as it raised allegations relating to the Paris 2024 Olympic weigh-in, anti-doping whereabouts, temporary retirement and her participation in two weight categories during the 2024 selection trials.
The second notice was issued to her for alleged misconduct at the Asian Games Selection Trials in May.

briefs.headline: Nemesis No. 1! Mitchell Santner scripts history, enters record books against India
briefs.deck: Mitchell Santner etched his name in history as the top wicket-taker against India in T20 internationals, achieving 32 dismissals. This remarkable feat occurred during the fourth T20I, where he claimed two wickets. He also celebrated reaching the 150-wicket milestone in T20Is. With a dominant 87-run victory, New Zealand earned their first win of the series, narrowing India's lead to 3-1.
briefs.bodyText:
New Zealand captain 
Mitchell Santner
 etched his name in the record books during the fourth T20I against India in Auckland on Friday, becoming the leading wicket-taker against India in the shortest format.
Santner achieved the landmark after dismissing Nitish Kumar Reddy, taking his tally to 32 wickets in 31 T20Is against India. He surpassed compatriot Ish Sodhi, who has claimed 30 wickets, to move to the top of the list.
Most T20I wickets vs India
- 31 Mitchell Santner
- 30 Ish Sodhi
- 24 Chris Jordan
- 22 Jofra Archer/Adil Rashid
Santner's latest scalp also marked another milestone in his T20I career as he became only the third New Zealand player to reach 150 wickets in the format. He now has 151 wickets from 142 matches at an average of 23.09, including four four-wicket hauls and best figures of 4/11.
Mitchell Santner's tally against India includes two four-wicket hauls, with his best figures being 4/11. Australia's Chris Jordan follows with 24 wickets, while England's Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid have 22 wickets each.
Santner returned figures of 2/24 in the fourth T20I, also dismissing Axar Patel, as New Zealand registered their first victory of the five-match series with an emphatic 87-run win. His nine wickets in the ongoing series have come at an average of 11.22.
Glenn Phillips
' blistering 107 off 49 balls and 
Michael Bracewell
's 65 off 25 powered New Zealand to 259/7, the highest T20I total against India. Jacob Duffy then claimed four wickets as India were restricted to 172/9, leaving the visitors with a 3-1 series lead ahead of the final match.

briefs.headline: Nitish Reddy joins unwanted list after horror outing against New Zealand
briefs.deck: In the fourth T20I against New Zealand, Nitish Reddy had a tough outing, giving away 64 runs and ranking as the second-most expensive bowler in T20I history for India. New Zealand set an impressive target of 259 runs, winning the match by 87 runs and narrowing India’s series lead to 3-1. Glenn Phillips played a vital role with his half-century, while India struggled to reach just 172 runs in…
briefs.bodyText:
Nitish Reddy entered an unwanted record list after an expensive outing with the ball in the fourth T20I against New Zealand in Auckland on Friday, conceding 64 runs to join an unenviable group of Indian bowlers.
Reddy's figures placed him alongside 
Yuzvendra Chahal
 and Varun Chakravarthy for the second-most expensive spell by an Indian bowler in T20I cricket. Krishna tops the list with 68 runs conceded against Australia in Guwahati in 2023, while Chahal had leaked 64 against South Africa in Centurion in 2018. Chakravarthy also conceded 64 against England at the Wankhede in 2026.
Reddy's expensive outing came as New Zealand piled up a mammoth 259/7 after being asked to bat first. The hosts eventually secured an emphatic 87-run victory, reducing India's series lead to 3-1.
The all-rounder was particularly targeted by Glenn Phillips, who smashed him for 32 runs in the 16th over, including four consecutive sixes. Phillips brought up his half-century in 31 balls before accelerating to a 49-ball 107, his third T20I hundred.
Reddy eventually dismissed Phillips after the New Zealand batter had crossed the three-figure mark, but the damage had already been done.
Phillips and Michael Bracewell (65 off 25 balls) added 115 runs off just 41 deliveries for the fifth wicket, powering New Zealand to the highest T20I total against India.
Most runs conceded by India in overs 11-20 in a T20I
151 South Africa Guwahati 2022
150 New Zealand Auckland 2026
146 England Southampton 2026
India's bowling struggles were not limited to Reddy. The visitors conceded 151 runs in the middle overs (11-20), the second-most by India in that phase of a T20I.
South Africa hold the record with 151 runs in Guwahati in 2022, while New Zealand's 150 in Auckland took the second spot in the list, followed by England's 146 in Southampton in 2026.
India's reply never gathered momentum as Jacob Duffy struck twice in the opening over, removing Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan. The visitors eventually finished at 172/9, suffering an 87-run defeat.

briefs.headline: 'The Time Is Now': How Phillips turned a John Cena moment into India's nightmare
briefs.deck: Glenn Phillips, during the fourth T20I against India, walked out to bat after Daryl Mitchell was dismissed off the fifth ball of the third over, bowled by Mayank Yadav. He first exchanged a fist bump with opening batter Finn Allen. As he began walking towards the crease, the DJ played The Time Is Now, John Cena's famous entrance theme.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The John Cena theme song playing in the background, 
Glenn Phillips
 walking out to the middle and then unleashing a stunning assault on India's bowlers. Eden Park witnessed a spectacle when the New Zealand batter arrived at the crease during the fourth T20I in Auckland on Friday.
Phillips walked out to bat after Daryl Mitchell was dismissed off the fifth ball of the third over, bowled by Mayank Yadav. He first exchanged a fist bump with opening batter Finn Allen. As he began walking towards the crease, the DJ played The Time Is Now, 
John Cena
's famous entrance theme.
What followed was absolute mayhem.
Phillips took the attack to the Indian bowlers and smashed a breathtaking 107 off just 49 balls. His innings included six fours and 10 sixes as New Zealand posted a massive 259/7.
Phillips and Bracewell take India apart
Phillips found an equally destructive partner in Michael Bracewell, who scored 65 off just 25 balls. The two batters added 115 runs off only 41 deliveries, taking New Zealand past the 200-run mark in the 16th over.
Phillips brought up his third T20I century, reaching the landmark in just 46 balls. His power-hitting left the Indian bowlers struggling for answers.
New Zealand finished with 259/7, their highest T20I total against India. 
They then bowled out the visitors' challenge, restricting India to 172/9 to secure an 87-run win.
India had already taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, but Phillips' innings helped New Zealand pull one back.
IPL lessons help Phillips find consistency
Phillips credited his time in the Indian Premier League for helping him improve his game. He is the leading run-scorer in the ongoing series, with 276 runs from four matches at an average of 92. His tally includes one century and two half-centuries.
The 29-year-old did not have a memorable IPL 2026 season with Gujarat Titans. He played only six matches and scored 67 runs, with 25 being his highest score.
However, Phillips said the experience gave him valuable lessons and opportunities to work on his batting.
“The IPL is a certain beast of its own and the balance of teams being one of eight overseas (players) with only four spots (in the eleven) make it quite tough. So, if you don't go out there and set the world on fire there's always another person waiting in line,” Phillips said in the post-match press conference.
He was happy with the facilities and coaching support he received at Gujarat Titans.
“At Gujarat, I was very lucky to have some unbelievable facilities, some great coaches and plenty of time to work (on his batting). I also showed in England as well being able to have volume (of runs) under the belt — whether it's red ball or white ball.
“Yes, you'd love to score runs in the IPL and you know make a load of cash and that would be fantastic but also there's a lot of learnings that you can take from that place (in the IPL) whether you're playing or not and I think that is also on each individual that is at the IPL or at any other tournament to be able to make the most out of where they go,” he added.
Phillips also had a productive Crowe-Thorpe Trophy earlier this year, scoring 181 runs in four innings at an average of 60, including a century. New Zealand won that series 2-1 against England.

briefs.headline: ‘I did everything I could for India’: Poonam Raut on retirement and unfinished dream
briefs.deck: After four years of chasing an India comeback, Poonam Raut has called time on her international career. In an exclusive conversation with TimesofIndia.com, the former India batter reflects on her retirement, the sacrifices her parents made to support her cricketing dream, her 86-run knock in the 2017 Women's World Cup final and the messages from young girls inspired by India's campaign. She also…
briefs.bodyText:
Poonam Raut
 spent four years trying to get back into the Indian team. She scored runs in domestic cricket, recovered from illness and worked towards a comeback. But the call never came.
Her last international appearance was in 2021. When Raut announced her retirement earlier this month, it was not because she had stopped wanting to play for India. It was because she had begun to realise that the return she had been working towards might not happen.
“I always had the desire to return to the Indian team,” Raut tells TimesofIndia.com. “Unfortunately, that didn't happen.”
Raut represented India for more than 12 years, scoring 2,299 runs in 73 ODIs. Her career included an 86 against England in the 2017 
Women's World Cup
 final and a world-record 320-run opening partnership with 
Deepti Sharma
 against Ireland that year.
India lost the World Cup final at Lord's by nine runs, but the campaign helped change how women's cricket was viewed in the country. For Raut, the memories go beyond the runs. She remembers messages from young girls whose parents had begun encouraging them to play cricket after watching India.
Her own journey began when women's cricket offered few guarantees of a career. Her father needed financial help from his employer to buy her first cricket kit. 
Now, having stepped away from international cricket, Raut wants to concentrate on coaching and mentoring the next generation.
In an exclusive conversation with this website, she speaks about the comeback that never materialised, the people who supported her and the innings that helped inspire a generation.
Excerpts:
After playing international cricket for more than 12 years, your last appearance for India came in 2021. What happened over the last four years that eventually led to your retirement?
My only aim over these four years was to make a comeback. I had two very good domestic seasons, finished among the leading run-scorers and performed well in multi-day cricket. But I couldn't get selected, and that's fine.
The selectors are focusing on youngsters, and I felt it was becoming difficult to continue at this stage of my career. Since childhood, my dream was to represent India. I lived that dream and achieved my goal. I did everything I could for the country, although I always wanted to return to the team.
Before last year's domestic season, I suffered from dengue, followed by pneumonia. I had a lot of joint pain and struggled to recover. I worked hard to regain my fitness, but I realised my body wasn't recovering the way it used to. That also contributed to my decision.
I have been mentoring young cricketers for four years. Many were 10-12 when I started working with them; today, they are 14-15 and approaching the competitive level. I felt that if I continued playing for another two or three years, I might not be able to give them the time they need at this crucial stage.
It was a very difficult decision. When you've played cricket for so long, retiring is never easy.
Poonam Raut Retirement Note
I am very grateful that I could contribute when India needed it the most. The result didn't go our way, but I feel we gave everything we had. That's how sport is sometimes.
I also scored a hundred against Australia and contributed against Pakistan. I was among India's leading run-scorers in that World Cup. Whatever I had to give, I gave everything in that tournament.
At that time, there wasn't much money in women's cricket, and not many people watched it. But the way we played changed the perspective of a lot of people.
The night before the final, I couldn't sleep, so I opened Facebook and Instagram and started reading the messages I had received. There were messages from young girls and senior citizens. I became very emotional.
Poonam Raut 86
A lot of girls told me they were able to play cricket because of us. Some said their fathers had encouraged them to take up the sport after watching our performances. Imagine parents who had earlier refused to let their daughters play cricket now encouraging them to pursue it.
Some girls even told me they wanted to cut their hair like Poonam Di!
There were elderly people who had sent their blessings and prayers as well. Reading those messages made me realise that we had genuinely brought about a change.
You made your India debut at a time when women's cricket did not enjoy the recognition it receives today. How difficult was it to pursue that dream, especially when it came to convincing your parents and getting the necessary support?
It was very difficult. My parents supported me at a time when cricket was barely considered a career option for girls.
Despite that, they never doubted me or asked me to reconsider. I told them I loved the game so much that I could play the entire day without getting tired of it.
The very next day, my father took me to buy a cricket kit and enrolled me in coaching. His financial situation wasn't particularly strong. During the 2017 World Cup, he told me that his boss had helped him financially when he needed money for my kit and coaching.
You won't believe how much that kit meant to me. The moment I got it, my excitement doubled. Everything I had watched on television suddenly became real.
Poonam Raut Childhood
I used that kit carefully for around five years because I knew how special it was. The bat, pads and helmet meant so much to me because they represented the beginning of my journey.
My parents also faced criticism from people around them, but they continued supporting me. They believed in me, and that played a huge role in helping me reach the Indian team.
Indian women's cricket has made significant progress, with the team winning the 2025 World Cup. Having seen the game evolve over the years, where do you think Indian women's cricket still needs to improve to achieve sustained dominance at the global level?
We have the talent to dominate women's cricket, and I am confident the day will come when we consistently dominate teams such as Australia, South Africa and England.
One major reason for my confidence is the support the BCCI is providing. The girls are getting more matches and opportunities than ever before. Earlier, we would play one or two international series in a year and then go straight into a World Cup. That is no longer the case. The team now plays throughout the year and gets more exposure against different opponents.
The Women's Premier League has also made a tremendous difference. Many players who have represented India have benefited from the platform it provides.
The pathway from domestic cricket to the international level has improved, too. Players get opportunities through the WPL, India A matches and age-group tournaments. The Under-19 Women's World Cup and state-level premier leagues are creating more opportunities for young cricketers.
Poonam Raut with Jhulan Goswami
Harmanpreet has done a tremendous job as captain. She led India to the Women's World Cup title, which is a historic achievement, and deserves a lot of credit.
Smriti has also shown what she can do as a leader. She captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru to the WPL title, which was a significant achievement.
I believe Smriti can do very well for India. She has the confidence to lead, and I have always felt that she tends to bat even better when she has the responsibility of captaincy. She has the experience, ability and temperament to take the team forward.
Poonam with Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana
Deepti opened with me for the first time because Smriti was injured. We were playing a quadrangular series, and Smriti was undergoing rehabilitation ahead of the World Cup.
We were both focused on preparing well for the World Cup. We wanted to give India a good start, and that was our priority throughout the innings.
That series was special for me because I had made a comeback to international cricket. I had been dropped in 2016 and spent around eight to 10 months away from the team. During that period, I played domestic cricket and scored plenty of runs.
When I returned, I wanted to make the most of the opportunity and contribute to the team's success. Deepti, despite being younger, responded very positively. She was a good partner to bat with.
Poonam Yadav with Deepti Sharma
For now, I am focusing on what is in my hands. I am enjoying my work with youngsters and want to continue doing that.
There will be opportunities in the future, whether in commentary, selection, administration, coaching or mentoring. I am open to exploring them, but at the moment, I am happy with what I am doing.
Working with young players gives you time to develop them properly. You can work on their technical skills, tactical understanding and mindset. When you see them improving and eventually achieving success, the satisfaction is incredible.
Poonam Yadav coaching
Success doesn't come overnight. You have to spend time working towards it, sometimes for years, before you begin to see results.
Many youngsters tell me they want to play state cricket next year or make it to the WPL as quickly as possible. But that's not how sport works. You need to be patient and understand that development takes time.
If you want to pursue cricket or any other sport professionally, you have to be disciplined and committed. Don't look for shortcuts. Don't run after success. Be patient, believe in yourself and keep working hard.
Poonam Raut career by numbers
I am extremely grateful to all my fans and well-wishers. When I announced my retirement, I received so many messages, and I was genuinely overwhelmed by the love and support.
I am also thankful to the media for acknowledging my performances and recognising my contribution to Indian cricket. I feel fortunate to have such a wonderful fan following.
I will continue to stay connected with my fans through Instagram and other social media platforms. I hope to share my experiences, connect with people and add value in whatever way I can.
Please continue to love and support me like this. I am truly grateful to all of you.

briefs.headline: 'Not doing justice': Yuvraj Singh wants Abhishek and Sooryavanshi in ODIs
briefs.deck: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes young batters Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi deserve more opportunities in 50-over cricket. Yuvraj feels that not regularly considering these players for the ODI team does not do justice to their talent. He also hopes they get a place in the squad soon.
briefs.bodyText:
Former India all-rounder 
Yuvraj Singh
 believes young batters 
Abhishek Sharma
, 
Ishan Kishan
 and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi deserve more opportunities in 50-over cricket.
Yuvraj feels that not regularly considering these players for the ODI team does not do justice to their talent. He also hopes they get a place in the squad soon.
"I would love to see him (Abhishek) in the ODIs, to be honest, and I have said this before that if we are not picking guys like Ishan Kishan, Abhishek and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in 50-over cricket, then somewhere down the line we are not doing justice to their talent," Yuvraj told PTI on the sidelines of an event.
Yuvraj has been Abhishek's mentor for several years and has played an important role in the youngster's development.
However, the former India all-rounder understands that the presence of experienced players makes it difficult for youngsters to find a place in the team.
"I understand we have some great players and it is hard to make a spot for them. I think the way they (young batters) are performing, hopefully, they should be in the squad soon. Whatever he (Abhishek) has achieved is because of his hard work, and credit goes to him," he added.
Abhishek responds to Yuvraj's 12-ball fifty challenge
Abhishek may have looked up to Yuvraj while growing up, but the young India opener is not ready to accept his mentor's challenge of scoring a half-century off just 12 balls.
The left-hander made his point after smashing a 38-ball 113 against New Zealand in the third T20I on Tuesday. His innings helped India register a six-wicket win, and he was named Player of the Match.
Yuvraj had posted a playful message on social media, saying that he was still waiting to see Abhishek score a fifty off 12 balls.
However, Abhishek said such an achievement was not easy and was not something batters planned for.
"I don't know what cricket he was playing back at that time, but it's not that easy at all," Abhishek said during the presentation ceremony.
"I would say if any batter wants to go there and bat like that, it's not easy at all. You can't just go and score 50 off 12 balls. It just happens once in a while," he added.

briefs.headline: India at 50: Celebrating a milestone for women’s cricket
briefs.deck: It was on October 31 in 1976 that the first women’s Test between India and the West Indies got underway at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Saturday marks a less remembered but a significant half century for Indian sport.
It was on October 31 in 1976 that the first women’s Test between India and the West Indies got underway at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. In the 50 years since, India may have played only 42 Tests more, and that is an issue no doubt, but women’s cricket has changed beyond recognition, with teams across the world getting to play so many limited-overs games right through the year.
It was only on Wednesday that India played Zimbabwe in an ODI at Vadodara. On the same day at Kochi the WPL’s mini auction was held. A 15-year-old Uma Kashvi was picked up by Delhi Capitals for ₹10 lakh. G. Kamalini, three years older, was bought by Gujarat Giants for ₹40 lakh.
And watching the auction was Shubhangi Kulkarni, as a member of the BCCI Apex Council. There had been little money in women’s cricket till not so long ago.
Shubhangi was one of India’s stars from that Test against the West Indies. With her leg-spin, she took five for 48 in the first innings, and two for 28 in the second.
She also had a hand in the first two wickets the visiting side lost in the first essay. She caught opener Gloria Gill at slip off the bowling of left-arm spinner Sharmila Chakraborty and played a part in the run out of Louise Browne.
“It was a dream beginning to my Test career, and a day I will always cherish,” Shubhangi told The Hindu. “Before the series, we had attended a coaching camp conducted by Lala Amarnath. I had learnt a few new tricks from him and from my coach, Kamal Bhandarkar, and was really looking forward to trying them out on the international stage.”
Those tactics worked. The match was drawn. As were the following two Tests at Chennai and New Delhi, but India won the fourth at Patna.
Shubhangi took seven wickets in India’s first-ever win in international women’s cricket. In a low-scoring match, the only fifty was scored by India’s wicketkeeper-opener Fowzieh Khalili, who made 58 in the first innings.
“What made the experience even more special was playing in front of a packed stadium,” recalls Shubhangi. “After the match, the crowd surrounded our bus and simply wouldn’t let it move!”
The women’s game, though, has moved on. And what a 50!

briefs.headline: ISL: Vinith’s stoppage-time goal earns BFC a point
briefs.bodyText:
Substitute Vinith Venkatesh’s injury-time equaliser salvaged a point for Bengaluru FC as it held NorthEast United FC to a 1-1 draw in the Indian Super League at the Indira Gandhi Stadium here on Friday.
Vinith’s right-footed strike into the bottom-left corner in the third minute of stoppage time cancelled out M.S. Jithin’s goal in the 15th minute. Vinith’s goal was a result of a defensive mix-up between ’keeper Gurmeet Singh and Eneko Satrustegui while Jithin’s opener came courtesy a counter-attacking move.
The draw maintains both teams’ unbeaten records, as NorthEast continues its position atop the table with eight points from four matches and BFC is second on seven points from three games.
NorthEast next plays Goan club Churchill Brothers away on November 5 while BFC will take the field a day later at the same Fatorda Stadium in Margao, where it faces FC Goa.
The result: NorthEast United FC 1 (Jithin 15) drew with Bengaluru FC 1 (Vinith 90+3).
